$comment: CMS-0057-F acceptance scenario manifest. It holds each scenario's id, name, capability and external-core (Augment) status per backend. It does NOT hold the Cloud Health Office (Replace) status: that comes from docs/epa-gap-matrix.md §11, and tools/Cms0057Evidence fails if a scenario here declares 'replace'. The acceptance suite validates its [Trait("Scenario",...)] against this file (see ScenarioManifestTests). Statuses are one of: PASSABLE, PARTIAL, GAP, N/A. The integration scored is 'filedrop': a plan keeps its core and UM system and feeds CHO their daily extracts (CPCDS and the authorization import), the default way a core connects (docs/integration/CORE-INTEGRATION-OPTIONS.md). Live core connectors (qnxt, facets, healthedge) are optional and are not scored until one is built for a plan.

capabilityDefinitions.PASSABLE: The repository's defined acceptance scenario is supported by the tested implementation. Not a CMS certification and not by itself production readiness for a specific payer deployment.
capabilityDefinitions.PARTIAL: Core of the scenario is implemented; some part is engagement or roadmap work.
capabilityDefinitions.GAP: Not implemented in the tested code; tracked so it is not silently claimed.
capabilityDefinitions.N/A: The scenario has no dependency on this backend/dimension.

filedrop.rationale: Coverage requirements are answered from CHO's prior-authorization rule set on the same CRD path as Replace. The rules are loaded with the PA rules importer, not from the daily drop.
DTR questionnaires are CHO's own; no core data is involved.

A PAS request is recorded and decided in CHO. The file drop flows one way, into CHO, so it cannot place the request in the plan's own UM system. That needs write-back (the optional live connector) or the plan working the request in CHO.

Authorizations decided in the plan's UM system and loaded by the authorization import (CSV or X12 278, through the drop) are the records the PA status reads, read-only (docs/integration/AUTHORIZATION-IMPORT.md). Not yet exercised by a file-drop acceptance test; the Replace limits apply.
An imported denial keeps the UM system's coded reason and its words; PAT03_FileDrop shows it reaching the member. The PAS response and X12 reason-code conformance limits are the same as Replace.
Decision clocks belong to the system that decides. Imported decisions are read-only in CHO and are not tracked by its deadline watchdog; their received and decision dates feed METRICS-01.
CDex additional-information exchange is CHO's own workflow.

scenarios.name: Drug exclusion from medical PA scope

filedrop.rationale: Drug exclusion is applied by CHO to whatever it serves; no core dependency.

scenarios.name: Provider Access — attributed member data pull

filedrop.rationale: Claims from the CPCDS drop and authorizations from the authorization import are served to attributed providers through the same projections as Replace. Same limits as Replace; clinical data is not in the drop (see PAT-02).

Claims the core adjudicated, loaded from the CPCDS drop, carry the billing and rendering NPIs and member ids the claims-history attribution reads (PROV02_FileDrop). A PCP panel still comes from configuration, not the drop.
The opt-out is recorded in CHO's consent registry, not the core.
The member, coverage and claims a requesting payer receives come from what the drop loaded. Not yet exercised by a file-drop acceptance test; clinical data is not in the drop.
Outbound initiation uses the member and coverage the drop loaded. Not yet exercised by a file-drop acceptance test; the Replace limits apply.
Opt-in is recorded in CHO's consent registry, not the core.
$member-match searches the members and coverage the CPCDS member and coverage files load (enrollment import). Not yet exercised by a file-drop acceptance test; the Replace limits apply.

scenarios.name: Patient Access — member claims / CARIN EOB

filedrop.rationale: Claims the core adjudicated, loaded from the CPCDS drop by the real importer, reach the member as CARIN BB EOBs on the same path as Replace (PAT01_FileDrop). Stays PARTIAL for the Replace reason: no external conformance run against CHO as a server.

The drop carries no clinical data. Clinical resources are served only from Payer-to-Payer imports today; a clinical file (FHIR NDJSON) in the drop is planned (docs/integration/CORE-INTEGRATION-OPTIONS.md).

Authorizations the plan's UM system decided, loaded by the authorization import, reach the member as PDex prior-authorization EOBs with their decision and denial reason, and only their own (PAT03_FileDrop). PARTIAL for the Replace reason: no profile validation.
SMART and OAuth are CHO's own; no core dependency.
The consent registry is CHO's own.
Metrics are computed from the UM system's own received and decision dates on imported authorizations (METRICS01_FileDrop). PARTIAL for the Replace reason: appeal outcomes are not yet linked.
